hypothesis: Source-native local associations learn elementary six-bit causal transitions from public counterfactual probes then compose novel three- and five-step sequences while retaining separate worlds. An equally informed conventional GF(2) affine solver is a strong novelty veto.
learner: Each of three operators in each world receives seven public before/action/after interactions on inputs [0,1,2,4,8,16,32]. Native stores observed output for each and derives bitwise affine influences from those observations, then computes multistep outcome by repeated application. No simulator secrets/seed shown to learner.
splits: FIT worlds 401-404, CHECK 801-802, DEV 901-904, every world has same 21 public calibration actions before any composed heldout sequence. Interleave worlds to test memory interference.
control: Independent conventional exact GF2-affine solver, 1NN single-step, single-step-only and cross-world-memory ablations. Same public action consequences and experience budget.
qualification: Native >=60/64 novel terminal predictions, >=10 per DEV world, >=24 beyond no-composition, exact two-OS-process science. A tie with conventional GF2 is NO native architecture superiority or Pareto advantage.
limitation: The structure is supplied as an affine-composition inductive bias. This is a constructed micro-world, not MiniGrid, not open-world learning, and not a new general intelligence mechanism.
